Water Heater Repair & Installation questions

My water heater is leaking. Do I actually need a new one?

If it is weeping from the tank seam, yes - a tank leak is not repairable. If it is dripping from the T&P valve, a fitting or the drain valve, that is a part, not a unit. Ask for the failure point in writing before you accept any replacement quote.

Do you replace the water heater itself, or only the heating side?

Confirm this with us on the phone. Our review record shows both patterns - one customer had the AC, furnace and water heater all replaced, another had us coordinate with their plumber while we handled the furnace adjustments the swap forced. Chicago licenses plumbing and ventilation separately, and we would rather tell you who does what up front.

Does a water heater replacement need a permit in Chicago?

Yes. The city recorded 445 permits mentioning water heater work in the 24 months to August 2026. Repairs and part swaps do not need one. If a contractor tells you a full replacement needs no permit, get another quote.

Is tankless worth it in a Chicago two-flat?

Often not, and the reason is the gas line rather than the appliance. Tankless draws far more gas at peak, so the line back to the meter usually has to be upsized - and in a masonry two-flat that run is the expensive part. Ask for the gas line assessment before you compare appliance prices.

How fast can you get here if there is no hot water?

Same day is common in our review record and next morning is the norm. We do not publish a guaranteed response window, and you should treat any contractor who does with suspicion in a Chicago January.

Which Chicago neighbourhoods do you cover?

Chicago citywide, plus the near north and northwest suburbs. Ask us for our current municipal registrations before you book anything outside the city - we will give you the list rather than a marketing map.

My building is a pre-war two-flat. Does that change the job?

Usually yes. West Chicago township, covering Wicker Park and West Town, is 83.0% pre-1940. In stock that age the masonry flue and the lack of duct routes are the variables that decide the price.

Do you work in condo buildings?

Yes, though associations frequently have their own rules on venting, roof access and shutoffs. Get those requirements in writing before you book anyone.

Chicago heating & cooling library

Chicago housing stock

Cook County Assessor data for the eight townships covering Chicago: 439,398 assessed properties - 305,736 single-family, 133,662 multi-family.

335,769 run a warm air furnace and 98,849 run hot water or steam. 306,261 have no central A/C at all, against 133,080 that do. 324,305 have a full basement.

Age is the variable that decides most jobs. West Chicago township - Wicker Park and West Town - is 83.0% pre-1940, the oldest stock in the city. Jefferson township, the bungalow belt, is the largest at 112,923 properties with a median year built of 1927.

What actually needs a permit

Chicago issued 62,810 permits of all types in the 24 months to August 2026. 4,888 mention HVAC work - about 204 a month.

Equipment replacement needs a permit. Repair, diagnosis, maintenance and refrigerant work do not. That is why the permit file records almost none of the HVAC work that actually happens in this city.

It also means a contractor's permit count measures their construction volume, not their service volume. 1,539 firms pulled a Chicago HVAC permit in those 24 months. Most of them will never take a no-heat call in January. Read a permit boast for what it is.

Where we work

Chicago, plus the near north and northwest suburbs.

We are not going to print a coverage map listing suburbs we cannot evidence a current registration for. Municipal registration is checkable and it lapses. Ask us which suburbs we are currently registered in and we will tell you the list.

The shared flue problem

This is the water heater issue specific to Chicago's building stock, and the reason a heating company should look at your swap.

In a typical bungalow or two-flat the furnace and the water heater both vent into one masonry chimney sized for the pair. Replace the water heater with a power-vent unit that exits a sidewall, and the furnace is left venting alone into an oversized, cold flue. Gases cool, condense, and attack the liner. At worst the furnace spills combustion products into the basement.

The fix is usually a correctly sized liner. It is cheap when planned and expensive when discovered. A quote covering only the appliance and the water connections is an incomplete quote.

sections.html:
Water Heater Repair & Installation questions

My water heater is leaking. Do I actually need a new one?

If it is weeping from the tank seam, yes - a tank leak is not repairable. If it is dripping from the T&P valve, a fitting or the drain valve, that is a part, not a unit. Ask for the failure point in writing before you accept any replacement quote.

Do you replace the water heater itself, or only the heating side?

Confirm this with us on the phone. Our review record shows both patterns - one customer had the AC, furnace and water heater all replaced, another had us coordinate with their plumber while we handled the furnace adjustments the swap forced. Chicago licenses plumbing and ventilation separately, and we would rather tell you who does what up front.

Does a water heater replacement need a permit in Chicago?

Yes. The city recorded 445 permits mentioning water heater work in the 24 months to August 2026. Repairs and part swaps do not need one. If a contractor tells you a full replacement needs no permit, get another quote.

Is tankless worth it in a Chicago two-flat?

Often not, and the reason is the gas line rather than the appliance. Tankless draws far more gas at peak, so the line back to the meter usually has to be upsized - and in a masonry two-flat that run is the expensive part. Ask for the gas line assessment before you compare appliance prices.

How fast can you get here if there is no hot water?

Same day is common in our review record and next morning is the norm. We do not publish a guaranteed response window, and you should treat any contractor who does with suspicion in a Chicago January.

Which Chicago neighbourhoods do you cover?

Chicago citywide, plus the near north and northwest suburbs. Ask us for our current municipal registrations before you book anything outside the city - we will give you the list rather than a marketing map.

My building is a pre-war two-flat. Does that change the job?

Usually yes. West Chicago township, covering Wicker Park and West Town, is 83.0% pre-1940. In stock that age the masonry flue and the lack of duct routes are the variables that decide the price.

Do you work in condo buildings?

Yes, though associations frequently have their own rules on venting, roof access and shutoffs. Get those requirements in writing before you book anyone.

sections.html:
Chicago heating & cooling library

Chicago housing stock

Cook County Assessor data for the eight townships covering Chicago: 439,398 assessed properties - 305,736 single-family, 133,662 multi-family.

335,769 run a warm air furnace and 98,849 run hot water or steam. 306,261 have no central A/C at all, against 133,080 that do. 324,305 have a full basement.

Age is the variable that decides most jobs. West Chicago township - Wicker Park and West Town - is 83.0% pre-1940, the oldest stock in the city. Jefferson township, the bungalow belt, is the largest at 112,923 properties with a median year built of 1927.

What actually needs a permit

Chicago issued 62,810 permits of all types in the 24 months to August 2026. 4,888 mention HVAC work - about 204 a month.

Equipment replacement needs a permit. Repair, diagnosis, maintenance and refrigerant work do not. That is why the permit file records almost none of the HVAC work that actually happens in this city.

It also means a contractor's permit count measures their construction volume, not their service volume. 1,539 firms pulled a Chicago HVAC permit in those 24 months. Most of them will never take a no-heat call in January. Read a permit boast for what it is.

Where we work

Chicago, plus the near north and northwest suburbs.

We are not going to print a coverage map listing suburbs we cannot evidence a current registration for. Municipal registration is checkable and it lapses. Ask us which suburbs we are currently registered in and we will tell you the list.

The shared flue problem

This is the water heater issue specific to Chicago's building stock, and the reason a heating company should look at your swap.

In a typical bungalow or two-flat the furnace and the water heater both vent into one masonry chimney sized for the pair. Replace the water heater with a power-vent unit that exits a sidewall, and the furnace is left venting alone into an oversized, cold flue. Gases cool, condense, and attack the liner. At worst the furnace spills combustion products into the basement.

The fix is usually a correctly sized liner. It is cheap when planned and expensive when discovered. A quote covering only the appliance and the water connections is an incomplete quote.
